notes: Format « faits » (9f4fd230, 857,6 k, son record). Accroche neuve : « ADHD facts most people have never heard ». Faits vérifiés, sans médicament ni mort : (1) 1775, M. A. Weikard, « Der Philosophische Arzt » (Barkley & Peters, J Atten Disord, 2012) ; (2) ~5 % des enfants dans le monde (Polanczyk et al., Am J Psychiatry, 2007 : 5,29 %) ; (3) ~1 adulte sur 40 avec un TDAH persistant (Song et al., J Glob Health, 2021 : 2,58 %) ; (4) héritabilité ~74 % (Faraone & Larsson, Mol Psychiatry, 2019) ; (5) sucre : méta-analyse de 16 études, aucun effet sur le comportement (Wolraich et al., JAMA, 1995) ; (6) ratio garçons/filles ~2:1 chez l'enfant, plus faible chez l'adulte (Faraone et al., World Federation of ADHD International Consensus Statement, Neurosci Biobehav Rev, 2021) ; (7) 446 enfants (223 + 223), pic d'épaisseur corticale vers 10,5 ans contre 7,5 ans, « un retard plutôt qu'une déviance » (Shaw et al., PNAS, 2007). Ses chiffres sur l'espérance de vie et le suicide écartés.

slides.texte_overlay:
ADHD facts
most people have never heard

ADHD isn't new.
a german doctor described it
in a medical book in 1775

about 1 in 20 kids
around the world
have ADHD

and it doesn't always go away.
around 1 in 40 adults
still have it

it's one of the most
inherited conditions there is.
twin studies put it at about 74%

sugar doesn't make kids hyper.
a 1995 review of 16 studies
found no effect on behaviour

boys get diagnosed about
twice as often as girls.
in adults, the gap
gets much smaller

in a 2007 study of 446 kids,
the brain's outer layer peaked
in thickness about 3 years later
in kids with ADHD

the researchers called it
a delay, not a defect.
a different timeline,
not a broken brain

follow for ADHD facts
that actually have a source
